findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/authority-client.ts:408-424 buffers the jobs SSE with response.text() before parseRunnerJobsAvailableSse runs, so a normal long-lived text/event-stream body will not surface an early jobs.available event to the runner; it will wait until the body closes or the timeout aborts, then packages/main/src/core/authority-runner.ts:438-456 falls back to claim only after that wait. This keeps the signed claim authority boundary safe, but it means the CLI does not actually consume a persistent /v1/runners/{runnerId}/jobs/stream notification hint promptly; the smoke test only covers a bounded SSE-looking response that closes after the event, not a real long-lived stream.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 86a50393d: streamRunnerJobsAvailable now uses bounded body reader and returns on the first classifiable jobs.available event from a long-lived text/event-stream instead of waiting for response.text() close/timeout. Verified by smoke long-lived stream scenario and build.

findings.desc: authority-runner-client-smoke exercises a positive jobs.available SSE hint followed by a signed claim, but the fake claim response is {"job":null} and the smoke never asserts out.claimedJobId stays null or that ownership/authority is derived only from the claim response. A regression could populate claimedJobId from SSE jobIds while still preserving the tested GET-before-POST order and claim_job ok event, so CHK-001 adversarial no-overclaim coverage is incomplete. Add an assertion/scenario that positive SSE + null or failed claim does not produce claimedJobId/releasedJobId/authority completion, and only a JobSpec returned by the signed claim can create ownership.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 86a50393d: smoke asserts positive SSE jobIds plus signed claim {job:null} leaves claimedJobId and releasedJobId null, proving SSE is not ownership. Verified by authority-runner-client-smoke.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/authority-client.ts:413-424 awaits response.text() before parsing SSE. With a real long-lived text/event-stream response that writes event: jobs.available/data {"count":1,"jobIds":["job-1"]} and keeps the connection open, streamRunnerJobsAvailable returns kind=timeout/status=200 instead of available, so runLatticeAuthorityControlPlaneOnce waits for the timeout before signed claim rather than immediately attempting claim as CHK-001 requires. Repro command used in review: npm --prefix packages/main run build -- --pretty false, then a local node --input-type=module HTTP SSE probe returned {"kind":"timeout","ok":false,"status":200} after the event was sent.
